The declined, unknown-outcome and reconcile branches of WEB-012 and SVC-ORDER-PAYMENT-1 can only be tested against a fake. inquirePaymentStatus also says a background reconciler runs 'past a threshold' that is never given.

question: We propose that every tenant table holding operational data or personal data gets row-level security, either through its own venue or scope column or through its parent row. Only genuine shared reference data is exempt. Confirm or correct.
why: 920-row-level-security.sql puts a policy on 313 of 584 tenant tables. The other ~270 are labelled 'reference data', but they include all 4 pii tables, identity.principal, orders.order_line, wallet.gift_card and games.credit_ledger. permission-resolution.md 7.1 says every tenant-scoped table enforces RLS. We are fixing this ourselves, but it changes what one venue's staff can see of another's data.
blocks: The 'row-level security holds' Done-when on every MIG and SVC ticket. As the DDL stands, it cannot be met for these tables.
affects: Every tenant database table; all services
first_release: Yes: every MIG-* migration and the service tickets that read them
default: Confirm the proposal as written: no tenant or PII table is exempt from RLS.

question: For these first-release screens, should we build the feature the screen promises or drop the promise? (a) WEB-016 guest password sign-in: guests can register with a password, but no guest password login exists. (b) GST-047 forced or recommended app upgrade: nothing carries a minimum app version. (c) GST-070 guest cabana reservation: bookResource has been staff-only since 19 September. (d) GST-070 leaving a restaurant waitlist: guests can join but not leave. (e) WEB-010 applying a promo code to the cart. (f) WEB-028/WEB-029 venue contact details and a sold-out or closed signal.
why: Each screen's purpose or states promise something its linked contract cannot supply (for example, TenantAppStatus carries no contact, sold-out or app-version field). Most of the 143 one-offs in this group are missing fields we add ourselves. These six are scope calls.
blocks: Build and acceptance of WEB-016, GST-047, GST-070, WEB-010, WEB-028 and WEB-029.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, IdentityService, WhiteLabelService, FnbService, CatalogueService
first_release: Yes: WEB-016, GST-047, GST-070, WEB-010, WEB-028, WEB-029
default: (a) Add a guest password sign-in, since registration already takes a password. (b) Add a minimum supported app version to the app status. (c) Cabanas stay staff-booked and GST-070 becomes table-only. (d) Add a guest leave-waitlist. (e) Add apply-promo-code to the cart. (f) Add contact details and a sold-out/closed flag to the app status.
superseded: Part (c) superseded 29 September (rev 3 REV3-15, GAP-C2): cabanas, loungers and non-dining tables placed on an ingested venue map are chosen and bought by the guest, like seats. See docs/registers/rev3-decisions.md.

question: Three guest-facing rules we cannot settle from the package: (a) Table reservations: is there a deposit or no-show fee, and how much (open item CF-85)? (b) Face Pass enrolment (GST-069): which face-capture SDK and template format does the app use? (c) WEB-018 asks for an 'anti-screenshot' dynamic QR, which a browser cannot enforce. Is a rotating code with a visible countdown enough?
why: Most of the 92 one-offs here are contract defects we fix ourselves (renames, missing 409s, paging). These three were left open in the package: CF-85 is unanswered, no capture SDK is named, and WEB-018's note asks for something the web platform cannot do.
blocks: GST-070 booking and cancel messaging, GST-069 enrolment, WEB-018 ticket display.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, FnbService, AccessService
who: Client product (with client counsel for b)
default: (a) No deposit and no no-show fee in the first release. (b) The SDK of the facial-reader vendor you have contracted, named by you. (c) Rotating code with countdown. No screenshot blocking on web.
applied: applied 28 September, one value open: Face-capture SDK and template format are the client's contracted facial-reader vendor's; the client must name the vendor.
superseded: Part (a) superseded 29 September (rev 3 REV3-8b): the dining deposit ships as a venue option, off unless the venue enables it; basis and amount are venue configuration.

question: Where the package says two things, which is right? (a) GST-009 in-app payment: card only (screen notes) or card or wallet (flow F11)? (b) GST-022 stale wait time: hidden past a threshold (F21) or shown with a caveat (contract and screen)? (c) Seats per POS sale: at most 10 (POS-002) or up to 50 (CreateSeatHoldRequest)? (e) POS-007: which single mechanism approves a shift variance above the threshold? The package has three.

blocks: GST-009, GST-022, POS-002/POS-004 seat selection, POS-005 tender, POS-007 shift close.
affects: Guest App, POS, OrderService (shift, payments), SeatingService
first_release: Yes: GST-009, GST-022, POS-002, POS-004, POS-005, POS-007
default: (a) Card or wallet. (b) Shown with a caveat, as the contract says. (c) 10 per sale. (d) All five. (e) A supervisor accepts the variance on the till (acceptShiftVariance). The other two paths are removed.

question: Confirm these permission splits: (1) emergency announcements get a permission separate from ANNOUNCEMENT_PUBLISH; (2) approving and publishing a product get different permissions (today both are PRODUCT_CONFIGURE); (3) reading venue settings gets a read permission instead of TENANT_CONFIGURE; (4) procurement gets its own permissions instead of borrowing ORDER_*, PRODUCT_CONFIGURE and LEDGER_APPROVE; (5) cancelling an accepted F&B order needs void authority, not ORDER_MODIFY; (6) recording a no-sale drawer open gets its own permission instead of SHIFT_SUSPEND.

blocks: The role and permission matrix (default role templates are still pending) and every screen guard that uses these operations.
affects: IdentityService permissions, FnbService, Inventory procurement, TenancyService, POS guards
first_release: Yes: POS-004, POS-007, POS-021, POS-023 guards and SVC-FNB, SVC-TENANCY, SVC-ORDER-SHIFT-4
default: Yes to all six.

question: For each limit the contracts call 'configured', what is the default value, and is it set per tenant or per venue? The limits: resale window, exchange window, reschedule window, F&B recall window, cart hold extension length and maximum extensions, product variant ceiling, over-receipt tolerance, stock-count tolerance, cross-queue limit, shift variance threshold, journal approval threshold, dashboard tile budget, report inline-run threshold, marketing attribution window, and guest OTP attempt limit.
why: The contracts use 'configured limit/threshold/window' in at least 15 places, but name no setting, no default and no column. platform.venue_settings has no policy columns. We will add the settings, but the values are yours.
blocks: The 409/400 refusal paths of these operations cannot be built or tested without a value.
affects: OrderService, CatalogueService, FnbService, InventoryService, QueueService, LedgerService, ReportingService, MarketingService, IdentityService
first_release: Yes: SVC-ORDER, SVC-CATALOGUE, SVC-IDENTITY-GUESTAUTH and SVC-REPORTING tickets
who: Client operations (client finance for the variance and journal thresholds)
default: Each is a venue setting with a tenant-level default. We send a sheet with proposed values for you to correct.

question: We propose that the state models in states/*.yaml are the rule: an action not allowed from the entity's current state is refused. Will you review those models for orders, shifts, promotions, tenants, work orders and seat holds, and define what 'open', 'live', 'active' and 'settled' mean in each?
why: states/*.yaml list only the legal moves. Operations such as publishPromotion, cancelReservation, leaveQueue and suspendTenant name one bad state or none. The contracts also use 'open', 'live', 'active' and 'settled' without mapping them to status values. We will add the shared refusal (409 InvalidTransition). Which states allow each action is a business rule.
blocks: The refusal paths of about 30 operations across the first-release services.
affects: OrderService, CatalogueService, FnbService, PlatformService, ReportingService, VenueOpsService
default: Confirm the current state models as the rule. We send a one-page table of each status word mapped to its statuses for you to correct.

question: Define these rules that the contracts state but never spell out: (1) release rollout stages: what values 'stage' takes; (2) workstation health score: the formula and the warning/failure thresholds; (3) policies: which languages are required before a policy can be published; (4) what counts as a 'live app' in white-label; (5) promotions: what 'near-zero' combined discount means in conflict analysis; (6) AI provider keys: how long a replaced key keeps working (grace window); (7) bulk refunds: how the selection criteria combine; (8) system reports: editable (reporting.yaml:2424) or clone-only (deleteReport)? (9) F&B corrective actions: who an escalation goes to.
why: Each operation states a rule in one line of prose and leaves out how it works. For (8) the contract contradicts itself: system reports are 'editable and forkable rather than locked' in one place and 'cannot be amended, only cloned' in another.
blocks: The validation and refusal logic of the operations concerned.
affects: Platform ops, TenancyService, WhiteLabelService, CatalogueService (promotions), AiService, OrderService (refunds), ReportingService, FnbService
first_release: Yes: SVC-TENANCY, SVC-WHITELABEL, SVC-CATALOGUE-PROMOTION-1, SVC-AI-AI-1, SVC-ORDER-ORDERS-1
default: (1) canary, partial, full. (2) We propose a weighted score and send it for review. (3) English and Arabic. (4) An app with a published configuration. (5) We propose the net line price falling below a stated minimum. (6) 24 hours. (7) All criteria must match (AND). (8) Clone-only. (9) The venue's food-safety lead.

question: How does a TICVAI platform operator in the Platform Console (P09) act inside a tenant? Do they pick a tenant and act under an audited platform-staff grant, or only through a support role the tenant grants them?
why: P09 is hosted 'Control Plane, outside every cell', but ADM-005, 016, 017, 018, 031, 412 and 421 call tenant-scoped cell operations with no tenantId, gated by tenant permissions. serviceAuth covers only service-to-service calls. No document says how a platform operator is authorised inside a tenant.
blocks: The Platform Console screens that act on a tenant, and the authorisation model for platform staff.
affects: Platform Console (P09), White Label admin (ADM-016/017/018), IdentityService, WhiteLabelService
first_release: Yes: ADM-005, ADM-016, ADM-017, ADM-018, ADM-031, ADM-412, ADM-421
default: The operator picks a tenant, then acts under a time-boxed platform-staff grant. Every action is audited and visible to the tenant.

question: Define these CatalogueService rules: (1) publishPromotion refuses a 'near-zero' line price: what is the floor? (2) createPromotion refuses 'unsatisfiable' conditions: which combinations count? (3) createBundle: the rounding tolerance when allocating the bundle price to components, and whether list price is the variant's current price; (4) setPromotionVariants (A/B): must the weights sum to 100, and is there a minimum per variant? (5) joinWaitlist is offered only when 'genuinely sold out': do held seats and terminal leases count as sold? (6) updateChannelCapacity cannot go 'below what has already sold': do leased units and the oversell allowance count? (7) generateCouponCodes: are codes single-use by default, and must the number of assigned guests equal the quantity? (8) promotion budget caps: refused at checkout, or reported only?
why: catalogue.yaml and promotions.yaml state each rule in one line and leave it out of the schema. So the 400/409 paths cannot be built or tested.
blocks: The validation and refusal paths of these operations.
affects: CatalogueService (catalogue, promotions, bundles, capacity, waitlist)
default: (1) Zero or below. (2) We list the combinations for review. (3) Allocate proportionally to list price, with the rounding remainder on the first component; list price is the variant's current price. (4) Must sum to 100, no minimum. (5) Held seats count; leases count. (6) Leased units count; oversell does not. (7) Single-use by default; assigned guests must not exceed the quantity. (8) Refused at checkout.

question: Define these VenueOps rules: (1) queue feed: when is a feed 'healthy'? (2) wait times: what the 'category' filter means; (3) game play with too few credits: refuse it (409) or accept it and report it for reconciliation? (4) resource check-in: which returned condition makes the resource unavailable, and when does it block further bookings? (5) incident investigation notes: kept as a history or overwritten? (6) authority notifications: what happens for a non-reportable incident or a repeat notification? (7) path closures refuse to 'strand' a point: stranded from where (entrances)? (8) may a venue map with disconnected areas be published? (9) work order verification: who approves completed to verified? (10) media assets: what 'in use' means for sorting expired assets.
why: The VenueOps contracts (queue, games, resources, maintenance, venue-map, assets) state these rules in prose and leave the details undefined. recordGamePlay contradicts itself: it says 'reported for reconciliation' and also declares a 409 'Insufficient credits'.
blocks: The refusal and state logic of the cited operations.
affects: VenueOpsService (queue, games, resources, maintenance, venue map, assets)
default: (1) Last reading within the feed's expected interval. (2) Attraction category. (3) Refuse online; accept and report when it arrives from an offline device. (4) Damaged means unavailable and blocks bookings until inspected. (5) History (append). (6) Refused if not reportable; repeats are recorded. (7) From every public entrance. (8) No. (9) A supervisor other than the technician. (10) Referenced by live content.

question: Which business codes must be unique, and within what scope (tenant, region or venue)? Role code, event code, product and category code, supplier code, loyalty programme code, blacklist entry, asset tag, collection name, venue map point, table code.
why: No contract says a code is unique, and the tenant DDL has no UNIQUE constraint ('indexed and not constrained'). We will add the shared duplicate-code response. Which codes are unique, and where, is a business rule.
blocks: The duplicate refusal on every create/update of these entities, and the unique constraints in the DDL.
affects: IdentityService, CatalogueService, InventoryService, MarketingService, AccessService, VenueOpsService, FnbService
default: Configuration codes (roles, products, categories, suppliers, programmes) are unique per tenant. Asset tags, table codes and venue-map points are unique per venue.

question: (a) In a blind stock count, may the counting device see the expected quantity and the variance (enterCountLine returns both)? (b) Is settlement reconciliation daily (BO-043 'Daily Reconciliation') or monthly and file-based (listSettlements)? (c) Does marking an item unavailable (86) take effect on every terminal immediately, or on 'Save changes' (BO-140)?
why: Most of the 25 contradictions in this group are ours to fix. These three decide how the business works: a blind count that shows the variance is not blind, and two settlement cadences cannot both be right.
blocks: BO-079 stock count, BO-043 reconciliation, BO-140 availability.
affects: Venue Management back office, InventoryService, LedgerService, FnbService
default: (a) No: hidden until the count is submitted. (b) Daily per venue. (c) Immediately.

question: For each external integration, who is the vendor, and when do we get API documentation and sandbox access? The integrations: payment gateways (Stripe and Network International, CF-131), card tokenisation and hosted checkout, face matching, the parking vendor, a password breach check, the FX rate feed, Apple/Google wallet pass signing, and DNS/certificates for custom domains.

first_release: Yes: WEB-012, WEB-014, WEB-021, GST-009, GST-071 and the linked service tickets

question: (a) Are exchange rates set per region (as stored) or per venue (as the guest screens assume)? (b) When a returning guest's verified contact matches an existing profile, does the order attach to it automatically (ADR-0045, accepted 18 September) or does the guest decide (the contract, 23 September)?
why: Most items in this group are internal contradictions we fix. These two are business calls. ledger.fx_rate has region_id only while P02 treats rates as a venue's enabled currencies, and the accepted ADR-0045 and the later marketing contract disagree.
blocks: Currency display on guest screens (listFxRates), and guest checkout profile linking.
affects: LedgerService, MarketingService, Guest App, Guest Web
default: (a) Rates are set per region, and each venue picks which currencies it shows. (b) Attach automatically, as ADR-0045 accepted.

question: Define these OrderService rules: (1) setting a cart line quantity to 0: does it remove the line? (2) a cash lift is refused if it 'exceeds the counted float': counted when, and against what? (3) adjusting a deposit box float: is the amount a change (delta) or the new total? (4) closing deposit boxes: are counted figures required, and can one close with a mismatch? (5) resuming a held order: which choices does the cashier have (keep prices, reprice, discard)? (6) refund policy: must the thresholds be in ascending order, and what is the minimum refund window? (7) retail secondary authorisation: what credential does the second person give (PIN or password)? (8) visit reminders: one per booking or one per guest? (9) opening a deposit box: a total or a denomination count?
why: orders.yaml and shift.yaml state the intent in prose but leave out each operation's own rules. The agents read the raw contract, so these are gaps in the package, not in the tooling.
blocks: Validation and refusal paths for cart, cash, refund and reminder operations.
affects: OrderService (cart, orders, shift and cash, refunds, reminders), POS
first_release: Yes: SVC-ORDER-CART-3, SVC-ORDER-CASH-1, SVC-ORDER-SHIFT-1/2/5, SVC-ORDER-REFUND-1, SVC-ORDER-POLICY-1
default: (1) Yes, it removes the line. (2) Against the float counted at the last count, less lifts since. (3) Delta. (4) Required; a mismatch closes with a recorded variance. (5) Keep prices or discard. (6) Ascending; minimum 0 days. (7) PIN. (8) One per booking per guest. (9) Either; a denomination count takes precedence.

question: Define these F&B rules: (1) order handover: which outcomes apply to each service mode, and is a delivery location required for delivery? (2) moving a kitchen ticket up: the default priority when none is given; (3) cancelling an F&B order: from which statuses (only ordered or accepted?); (4) amending a sent order turns it into a void: which reasons may be given? (5) temperature and cold-chain logs: when does an out-of-range or missed reading open a corrective action, and at what severity? (6) notifying a table's server when none is assigned; (7) releasing a production plan: one task per line or grouped by station? (8) production stock: does it move at start or at completion? (9) recipe cost per portion: computed or entered? (10) substitution rules: tied to a menu item, a recipe or the whole venue? (11) an item tracked while ordered offline: what the conflict is.
why: fnb.yaml states intent in prose but leaves each of these rules unspecified. For (8) the contract and the production-run state model disagree.
blocks: Refusal and side-effect logic of the cited FnbService operations.
affects: FnbService, POS, Kitchen Display
first_release: Yes: SVC-FNB-ORDER-1, SVC-FNB-KITCHEN-1, SVC-FNB-BILL-1, SVC-FNB-GUESTORDERING-2/3, SVC-FNB-MODIFIER-1
default: (1) Collected or delivered for each mode; location required for delivery. (2) Top of the queue. (3) Ordered or accepted only; later is a void. (4) The void reason list. (5) Out-of-range opens high severity; a missed reading opens medium. (6) Goes to the outlet's supervisor. (7) Grouped by station. (8) At start, as the state model says. (9) Computed. (10) A recipe. (11) We propose: stock ran out while offline.

question: Define these IdentityService rules: (1) which changes to a staff member revoke their sessions at once (end date, primary role, permissions)? (2) guest session lifetime, and one session per device or shared? (3) delegation: who may grant delegated access, the minor age, and what happens when a date of birth is missing? (4) guest email verification: link lifetime and channel; (5) which MFA kinds staff may enrol (authenticator app, SMS, email)? (6) failed step-up: how many tries before lockout? (7) minimum password length floor for the password policy.

affects: IdentityService, Guest App, Guest Web, POS sign-in
who: Client security (client counsel for the minor age)
default: (1) All three. (2) 30 days sliding, one session per device. (3) The account holder grants; the minor age is the one counsel gives; a missing DOB is treated as a minor. (4) 24 hours, by email. (5) Authenticator app, plus email as fallback. (6) 5 tries. (7) 8 characters.
applied: applied 28 September, one value open: Minor age is the value client counsel sets; recorded as an open value, not assumed.

question: Define these accounting rules: (1) which posting event types must have an account mapping before a venue can trade? (2) partial forfeit of a deposit: is the remainder refunded to the guest? question: Define these rules: (1) approval matrix: a venue 'may tighten and never loosen' a higher rule. What counts as loosening (higher threshold, fewer approvers, a different approver role)? question: Do Menu Item, Merchandise Item, Inventory Item and SKU (a variant's code) go into the glossary as their own terms, or does everything become 'Product'?

question: How many previous passwords may a staff member not reuse? The policy defaults to 5, but only 'same as the current one' is refused today.

blocks: MFA enrolment and removal rules, and the identity DDL.

default: By permission. The list is ROLE_MANAGE, LEDGER_APPROVE and every platform-staff permission, and you may add to it.

question: Where a journey and its contract disagree, which is right? (a) F22: a failing brand colour contrast is warned (flow) or refused (setTheme)? (b) F22: is rollback 'one click' back to live, or restore, then review, then publish (restoreConfigVersion)? (c) F34: may a return without a receipt be looked up by card, membership or item and date, or only by receipt or order number? (d) F69: is incident handling part of maintenance or of workforce?
why: Flows F22, F34 and F69 contradict their own contracts on blocked vs warned, on publish vs draft, and on which lookups exist. The other contradictions in this group are ours to reconcile.
blocks: White-label theming and rollback (CMS-005, CMS-014, CMS-015), retail returns, incident screens.
affects: White Label CMS, WhiteLabelService, RetailService, VenueOpsService
default: (a) Refused. (b) Restore, then review, then publish. (c) Receipt or order number only in the first release. (d) Maintenance.

question: Which of these need a second person's approval, and who approves? Cancel a purchase order; close a purchase order short; close a stock transfer short; recount a stock count; start a release rollout; close a fiscal period; reopen a fiscal period; reopen a shift; cancel a performance; a retail return above a threshold.
why: The state models mark these transitions requiresApproval, but the package never says what that means: no approver, no approval request and no pending response. decisions-build-check.md already lists 26 such orphan flags. We will build the approval mechanism. Which actions use it is your call.
blocks: The approval path on each of these operations.
affects: InventoryService, LedgerService, OrderService (shift), RetailService, CatalogueService, Platform ops
default: Finance and procurement actions (close and reopen period, cancel or short-close a purchase order) go through the approvals engine to a finance approver. Shift reopen, stock recount and retail returns above the threshold need a supervisor's step-up on the same device. Rollouts need the platform release manager.

question: May screens say 'Booking' (Booking Confirmation, Group Booking) and 'Release hold', or must they use Order, Reservation and Entitlement as the glossary requires?
why: naming-and-style bans 'Booking' for Order and 'Booking, Hold' for Reservation. Yet WEB-013, GST-010, GST-028 and WEB-041 and the group-booking screens use them, and the package records no exception.
blocks: Screen labels and a possible glossary pass across screens, contracts and DDL.
affects: Guest Web, Guest App, back office, resources and orders contracts
first_release: Yes: WEB-012, WEB-013, WEB-031, WEB-041, GST-010, GST-028, GST-045
default: Allow 'Booking' in guest-facing labels as a recorded exception. Code and contracts use Order and Reservation.

question: Will you approve glossary definitions for the domain nouns the contracts already use: Attraction, Queue, Wait Time, Itinerary, Accreditation, Form, Settlement, Reconciliation, Report, Channel, Work Order, Segment, Campaign, Journey, Category and Tile?
why: The standard says 'a term in code that is not in the glossary is a review finding'. The draft glossary (about 40 terms, 'needs client sign-off') defines none of these.
blocks: Glossary sign-off. Until then, every contract using these nouns fails its own review rule.
affects: Glossary; all contracts and screens
first_release: Yes: GST-022, GST-051, WEB-004, CMS-001, BO-618
default: We draft each definition from the contracts and you approve it.

question: Can a guest raise a case (a complaint, lost property) while offline and have it sent later, or does raising a case need a connection?
why: raiseMyCase says 'works offline and queues'. F54 says a guest 'cannot raise a case' offline, and GST-034, WEB-034, WEB-025 and GST-068 say raising and replying need the connection. We will add the case kind and the guest thread read.
blocks: The offline state of the guest case screens, and the offline behaviour of raiseMyCase.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, MarketingService (cases)
first_release: Yes: GST-034, GST-040, GST-068, WEB-025, WEB-034
default: It needs the connection, as F54 and the four screens say. Offline, the screen shows how to reach staff in person.

question: Define these MarketingService rules: (1) wishlist: is the same product for two different performances one entry or two? (2) when 'offer at checkout' is off, is the match check skipped entirely? (3) guest documents: how long are they kept (retainUntil is described as required)? (4) merging two guests who each hold several loyalty programmes: how are points and tiers combined? (5) manual loyalty adjustments: which adjustment types exist, do they affect tier and lifetime points, and which report shows them? (6) chat handover to an agent: where do the queue position and wait estimate come from?
why: marketing-crm.yaml states each rule without the mechanism. The merge result, for example, carries a single loyaltyPoints number against per-programme positions.
blocks: Wishlist, guest profile merge, loyalty adjustment, document upload and handover tickets.
affects: MarketingService, Guest App, back office CRM
default: (1) Two. (2) Yes. (3) Until the purpose ends, then as counsel sets. (4) Per programme: points added, and the higher tier kept. (5) Goodwill, correction and expiry reversal; they affect the balance only, not tier or lifetime points; shown in the loyalty ledger report. (6) The live agent queue.
applied: applied 28 September, one value open: retainUntil = end of purpose + retention period counsel sets; the period per document kind is an open value (zero until named, i.e. delete at end of purpose). M

question: What format and scope should human-readable numbers have: order number, receipt number, case number, incident number, work order number, game card code? And which of them must be gapless for tax (CF-133)?
why: Each is a required field and a plain text column with no format, scope or generation rule, and the DDL has no sequences. CF-133 leaves the numbering scope for VAT invoices (legal entity, venue or till) and offline gapless numbering open. We will add the convention. The format and legal scope are yours.
blocks: Order, receipt, case and incident creation, including offline receipts on the till.
affects: OrderService, FnbService, RetailService, MarketingService, VenueOpsService, POS
who: Client finance (client counsel for tax invoices)
default: Server-assigned: a venue prefix plus a sequence per venue, with each till holding a reserved range for offline. Only tax invoices are gapless, per legal entity.

question: Pick one meaning for 'till': the Workstation (the device) or the Deposit Box (the cash drawer)? And may staff-facing labels say POS, drawer or float?
why: naming-and-style bans 'Till' under both Workstation and Deposit Box, and docs/glossary.md disagrees with it. Contracts and screens use 'Shift & Till', 'drawer', 'POS Profile' and 'tills'.
blocks: A single glossary, and the labels on the shift and cash screens.
affects: Glossary; OrderService (shift), POS, back office cash screens
default: Workstation is the device and Deposit Box is the cash drawer. Staff-facing copy may say 'till' for the Workstation. POS and drawer stay out of code.

question: Define these ReportingService rules: (1) the default maximum date range when a report sets none; (2) the default dates when none are given; (3) alerts list: the default status filter; (4) an 'outside range' alert rule: must both thresholds be set? (5) report history: who sees other people's report runs? (6) supplier performance (OTIF): what 'on time' and 'in full' mean, and against which timestamps; (7) scheduled reports: which fields each frequency needs, and whose time zone?
why: reporting.yaml states the intent but leaves out the rule each operation needs to validate or fail. For example, runReport's 400 'date range exceeds the limit' has no limit when maxDateRangeDays is null.
blocks: Report run, alert and schedule validation.
affects: ReportingService, back-office reports
default: (1) 366 days. (2) Today. (3) Open alerts. (4) Yes. (5) Venue managers see their venue's runs. (6) On time means received on or before the purchase order's expected date; in full means received quantity at least the ordered quantity. (7) The venue's time zone.

question: Define these WhiteLabelService rules: (1) app icons: which platforms and sizes are generated? (2) splash screen changes on web: immediate or at the next build? (3) policies list: current version only, or every version? (4) homepage sections: how each section maps to a module (tickets to ticketsAndBooking, and so on) when checking for disabled modules; (5) content pages and promo blocks: what may change after publishing, and must an end date follow the start date? (6) fonts: what 'Arabic enabled' means, and is a secondary Arabic face required? (7) scheduled publishing: what activates it at the scheduled time? (8) footer: is it set per tenant in the control plane or in the tenant's own configuration?
why: white-label.yaml states each rule in prose and leaves the behaviour open. For example, scheduledFor exists with no activation mechanism anywhere in the package.
blocks: Branding, homepage, content and publishing tickets.
affects: WhiteLabelService, White Label CMS
default: (1) The iOS and Android store sets, plus web favicons. (2) Immediate on web. (3) Current only, with history on request. (4) We publish the mapping for review. (5) Published pages may only be archived; end must follow start. (6) Arabic is listed in the tenant's languages; a secondary Arabic face is required whenever a secondary Latin face is set. (7) A scheduled job. (8) Tenant configuration.

question: Is a 'session' (Session Calendar BO-015, Session Template BO-016, 'how many people a session can take' BO-017, POS 'session time') the same thing as a Performance, or a separate concept that needs its own glossary entry?
why: The glossary bans 'Session' for Event and Performance, yet joinWaitlist, BO-015 to BO-017, POS and the resources manifest (/sessions/{sessionId}) use it. The manifest's sessionId points at no entity at all.
blocks: Screen names and the resources manifest model.
affects: Glossary; CatalogueService, resources, POS, back office
default: It is a Performance. Rename to Performance and hang the resources manifest off a Performance.

question: Is guest parking sold and paid in the app (GST-027 and WEB-041 'Reserve & Pay'), and do guests see live space availability, or is parking only an entitlement attached to an order paid elsewhere?
why: The access contract has only list/set facility and create/update entitlement. ParkingEntitlement requires an orderId, but GST-027 and WEB-041 link no order or payment operation, F50 promises a 'car park is full' check, and ParkingFacility has only a static capacity.
blocks: GST-027, GST-028 and WEB-041 build, and the parking contract.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, AccessService (parking)
default: Parking is sold through the normal cart and checkout (so the entitlement gets its orderId). No live availability in the first release: a full car park is shown only when capacity is reached.

question: Do guests sign in with enterprise SSO at all, and are guests offered a second factor at sign-in?
why: WEB-016 and GST-042 are wired to the staff login and SSO pair, which need a workstation, map groups to roles and return a staff session. WEB-016 also labels step-up MFA 'Second factor at sign-in'. Guests already have one-time code, social and UAE Pass sign-in returning a GuestSession.
blocks: WEB-016 and GST-042 sign-in, and SETUP-AUTH end to end.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, IdentityService
default: No SSO for guests and no guest MFA at sign-in. Guests use one-time code, social sign-in and UAE Pass.
superseded: Part 2 superseded 29 September (rev 3 GAP-B1): guest two-step verification is a per-venue setting, off by default. Part 1 stands: guests never use enterprise SSO.

question: What are the default and maximum hold lengths for: a seat hold (the contract allows 60 to 1800 seconds; POS copy says eight minutes), a cart capacity lease (30 to 3600 seconds), a merchandise reservation for collection, and a stored-value authorisation (default 300 seconds)?
why: The contracts make the client send the hold length, but nothing gives it a value, and the venue hold policy is provisional and unreadable. The only concrete figure is 'eight minutes' in POS screen prose. We will make the defaults readable. The values are yours.
blocks: Seat selection, cart and checkout, and shop-and-collect on guest and POS channels.
affects: SeatingService, CatalogueService (leases), RetailService, OrderService; POS, Guest App, Guest Web
first_release: Yes: POS-004, WEB-007, WEB-033, WEB-042, GST-026, GST-049
default: Seat hold 8 minutes, extendable to 30. Cart lease 15 minutes. Merchandise reservation until the end of the visit day. Stored-value authorisation 300 seconds.

question: Define these inventory rules: (1) may an item's category or preferred supplier be cleared? (2) rejecting received goods: by line (batch or expiry) or by item? (3) which requisition statuses count as 'approved' for editing lines? (4) stock movements: which kinds need a reason, and does the kind or the sign decide the direction? (5) what 'allocated' and 'available' stock mean; (6) a recount: does it replace the earlier count lines? (7) starting a stock count: are lines pre-filled from on-hand stock? (8) purchase order price: taken from the supplier quotation or entered, and how PO numbers are formed.
why: inventory.yaml leaves each rule unstated. For example, rejectReceivedGoods addresses lines by item only, although a receipt can hold one item on several batch lines.
blocks: Item, receipt, count, movement and purchase order operations.
affects: InventoryService, back-office inventory
default: (1) Yes. (2) By line. (3) Approved and later. (4) Adjustments and waste need a reason, and the kind decides the direction. (5) Allocated is reserved for orders; available is on-hand minus allocated. (6) Yes. (7) Yes, with blind counts hiding the figure. (8) From the quotation, editable with a reason; PO numbers per venue, in sequence.

question: At which level are these owned and seen? Upsell rules (created at region, deleted and listed at venue); suppliers (region or tenant) and supplier quotations (venue); a stock transfer between two venues, which both venues must see; and the approval matrix a venue sets (tenant, region or venue).
why: The operations declare a scope level that does not match where the row lives. promotions.upsell_rule has no scope column at all, and a cross-venue transfer sits at tenant scope, where neither venue can see it.
blocks: Upsell rules, supplier quotations, stock transfers and approval matrix setup.
affects: CatalogueService (upsell), InventoryService, TenancyService (approvals), OrderService (payment tokens)
default: Upsell rules are owned at region and read at venue. Suppliers are owned at tenant, and venues may quote against them. Both venues see a transfer between them. A venue sets only its own matrix, tighter than the level above.

question: When a cashier signs in on a till someone else holds, is the sign-in refused until a supervisor ends the other session, or does the new sign-in end it?
why: identity.yaml section 3.1.3, ADR-0004 and forceLogout say a second login is rejected (409) and only a supervisor force-logout ends it. The POS-000 note says signing in 'ends their session as terminated'. We will settle the session storage.
blocks: POS-000 sign-in and the session model in SVC-IDENTITY.
affects: IdentityService, POS
default: Refused, as section 3.1.3 says. A supervisor ends the other session, and POS-000 is reworded.

question: Does the itinerary planner (GST-051 to GST-054 and GST-059, with group sharing by QR, CF-92) ship in the first release?
why: CF-92 minuted it as agreed on 10 August, but the package has no itinerary schema, operation, table or on-device store. Every screen's openQuestions still say its endpoint has no matching operation. guest-parity-audit.md marks it 'app only (raise)', which means ask you.
blocks: GST-051, GST-052, GST-053, GST-054, GST-059 and flow F49.
affects: Guest App, AiService
first_release: Yes: GST-051, GST-052, GST-053, GST-054, GST-059
default: Defer it to a later release and take the five screens out of Block A, since nothing exists to build them against.

question: Confirm how each money event posts to the ledger: card payment, cash payment, refund, POS offline sync, loading game credits (a liability), and loyalty points accrual (no event type exists for it). Also, how is a journal entry number formed?
why: finance.yaml has account mappings by PostingEventType, a suspense account and fiscal periods. But createPayment and createRefund read neither the mappings nor the periods, loadGameCredits writes no ledger row, and entry_number has no format.
blocks: Payment, refund, sync, game-card and loyalty posting in the first-release services.
affects: LedgerService, OrderService, WalletService, MarketingService (loyalty)
first_release: Yes: SVC-ORDER-PAYMENT-1, SVC-ORDER-REFUND-1, SVC-ORDER-SYNC-1, SVC-WALLET-CARD-1, SVC-MARKETING-LOYALTY-1
default: Use the existing event types, plus two new ones: game credit loaded and points accrued. Entries post to the open period for the event date. Entry numbers run in sequence per legal entity per fiscal year.

question: Is 'Department' a canonical term (docs/glossary.md) or banned (the naming standard), and may 'zone' name physical areas such as dining zones, access zones and seating zones?
why: The two glossaries disagree on Department, and 'Zone' is banned for Operating Area although it names dining, access and seating areas across the contracts. We will accept OrgUnit (the 26 August rename) ourselves.
blocks: A single glossary, and the labels on BO-064 and POS-024.
affects: Glossary; workforce, tenancy, inventory, fnb, access contracts
default: Department is canonical. 'Zone' is defined as a physical area inside a venue.

question: For operations with an 'escalated' permission (bulk price change, menu publish and rollback, comping an item, merging guests, broadcasting to guests, setting fraud rules, setting role permissions and others), what makes an action escalate, and who holds the higher permission?
why: 14 of 25 escalated declarations repeat the base permission, so they gate nothing, and no document defines what escalation means. The only hints are 'an approval gate' and 'above the configured value'.
blocks: The escalation checks on these operations.
affects: CatalogueService, FnbService, WhiteLabelService, MarketingService, IdentityService
default: Escalate above a configured value threshold to a distinct manager permission. Where no threshold makes sense, drop the escalation.

question: Who decides which AI provider a tenant uses, and so where its data is processed: the tenant (ADR-0009), each region (the contract), or TICVAI platform staff on ADM-037?
why: setAiProvider calls the choice 'a residency decision' at region level. ADR-0009 calls it 'a per-tenant configuration with a compliance gate', and ADM-037 says 'which model a tenant uses'. The provider body cannot even express a region.
blocks: ADM-037 and the AI provider configuration (SVC-AI-CONFIG-1).
affects: AiService, Platform Console
default: Per tenant with a compliance gate, as ADR-0009 says. Platform staff set it on ADM-037, and a region may restrict the choice.

question: For a minor's Face Pass enrolment, how does the guardian consent in the app, and what age counts as a minor?
why: The contract says 'a minor's consent is given by a guardian' and guardianSubjectId is required for a minor. But GST-069 has no guardian step and nothing tells it the subject is a minor.
blocks: GST-069 and WEB-024 enrolment.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, AccessService (biometrics)
default: The signed-in adult enrols a linked child and is recorded as guardian. Counsel sets the age.
applied: applied 28 September, one value open: Counsel sets the age below which a subject is a minor; missing DOB counts as a minor meanwhile.

question: If the itinerary planner ships, may a guest ask the AI for a day plan? requestSuggestion currently refuses anything but prepPlan, upsell and waitTime from guests, while F49 uses kind=scenario.
why: requestSuggestion says 'a guest caller may ask for prepPlan, upsell and waitTime only', yet F49 step 4 on GST-054 builds the itinerary from kind=scenario. GST-052, GST-054 and GST-059 call it with no kind. This follows from the itinerary question (R187).
blocks: GST-052, GST-054, GST-059 and the guest AI rules.
affects: Guest App, AiService
default: Follow R187: if the planner is deferred, remove the itinerary suggestion from those screens. If it ships, add a guest-allowed itinerary kind.

question: May 'Kitchen Ticket' be its own glossary term (the order slip on the kitchen display), and may guest-facing copy say 'QR' (GST-055 'Dynamic QR Ticket')?
why: The glossary reserves Ticket for the entitlement instrument and bans 'QR' for Media Code. KitchenTicket is used throughout fnb.yaml, the DDL and the paths, with no glossary entry.
blocks: Glossary, and naming on the kitchen and guest ticket screens.
affects: Glossary; FnbService, Kitchen Display, Guest App
default: Yes to Kitchen Ticket as its own term. 'QR' is allowed in guest-facing copy only.

question: Define the AI rules the contract leaves open: (1) for each of the 13 suggestion kinds, what it bases the suggestion on and how much history is 'enough data'; only price and replenishment have a rule today. (2) how long an AI-proposed configuration change stays open before it expires, before and after approval; (3) which approval level each kind of generated configuration needs.
why: ai.yaml states heuristics for 2 of 13 kinds. The 422 'not enough data' has no threshold, and the proposed-to-expired timers have no duration anywhere in the package.
blocks: Suggestion, generate-configuration and expiry logic.
affects: AiService, back office, Guest App suggestions
default: (1) We draft a one-line rule and a minimum history per kind for you to correct. (2) Proposed: 7 days; approved but not applied: 24 hours. (3) Anything touching prices or permissions needs a manager; everything else needs the requester's own approval.

question: Define these subscription rules: (1) how the effective date and proration combine on a plan change, and whether upgrades are always immediate; (2) what status and renewal date a tenant's first plan gets; (3) may a suspended or terminated tenant's details be amended? (4) is a webhook subscription list per API client or per tenant?
why: subscription.yaml defines a downgrade only loosely and says nothing about effectiveFrom, prorate or first assignment. listWebhookSubscriptions says 'what this client is subscribed to' but serves staff with no client filter.
blocks: Plan assignment and change (SVC-PLATFORM-SUBSCRIPTION-1) and tenant updates.
affects: PlatformService (subscription, tenants, public API)
default: (1) Upgrades take effect immediately with proration; downgrades take effect at the next renewal. (2) Active, renewing one term from start. (3) Suspended yes, terminated no. (4) Per tenant, filterable by client.

question: Define these retail rules: (1) a barcode or SKU price check at a venue: which outlet's price and stock does it show, and is an inactive item 'not found'? (2) a merchandise reservation: the earliest and latest expiry allowed; (3) looking up a sale by several identifiers, or a receipt matching several sales: which wins?
why: retail.yaml leaves these out. Merchandise rows are per outlet, but lookupMerchandise is venue-scoped and returns one price 'at this outlet'.
blocks: POS retail price check, merchandise reservation and returns lookup.
affects: RetailService, POS
default: (1) The outlet of the workstation asking; inactive items are not found. (2) At least 15 minutes ahead and no later than the end of the visit day. (3) Receipt barcode first, then receipt number, then order number; several matches return a list.

question: Do 'Game Card' and 'Gift Card' stay as names (a recorded exception to 'never write Card' and 'Money Card'), or are they renamed to Media and Money Card?
why: The glossary bans Card for Media and 'Gift card' in favour of Money Card, yet games.yaml, wallet.yaml, the DDL and POS use GameCard, GiftCard and cardCode, and no exception is recorded.
blocks: Naming across games and wallet contracts, DDL and POS.
affects: Glossary; games and wallet contracts, POS, Guest Web
default: Keep Game Card and Gift Card as recorded exceptions, since guests know them by those names.

question: At an access gate, what does the podium operator set on SCN-016: the operating mode (normal, free flow, drop arm, closed, podium, maintenance), the turnstile mode (entry, re-entry, crossover, exit, free rotation, closed), or the direction? And which wins if they disagree?
why: AccessPoint carries operatingMode, mode and direction. setTurnstileMode is titled 'Set the operating mode' but writes only mode, and nothing writes operatingMode. SCN-016's own note says 'confirming the direction IS setting the mode'.
blocks: BO-064 and SCN-016 gate configuration and SVC-ACCESS-ACCESSPOINT-2.
affects: AccessService, back office access, scanner app
default: The podium sets the operating mode. Direction is fixed per access point. Turnstile mode is reduced to free rotation or closed within the operating mode.

question: May reason lists end in 'Other' if a note is then required, or must every reason be modelled? The lists include ticket reprint, cash withdrawal and holding a course.
why: The naming standard bans 'other' as 'a design gap wearing a name', yet about 39 enum values in the contracts are 'other'. The rule never says whether a catch-all reason with a free-text note is allowed.
blocks: The reason lists on POS reprint, cash and kitchen screens.
affects: OrderService, FnbService, POS, Kitchen Display
default: Allow 'Other' only with a required note, and review the notes quarterly to add real reasons.

question: When a supervisor overrides a denied scan, is the original denial kept and the override recorded separately, or is the denied scan updated in place? And may a Face Tag be read through the Face Pass lookup?
why: overrideAccess takes a new id (append) while scan_event carries override columns on the denied row (update), and nothing settles which. getFacePassEnrolment returns a kind that includes faceTag, with no rule.
blocks: The access override (SVC-ACCESS-SYNC-1) and Face Pass reads (SVC-ACCESS-ACCESS-2).
affects: AccessService, scanner app
default: Keep the denial and record the override as its own row. Face Tags are not returned by the Face Pass lookup.

question: Please confirm the UAE denomination list (values, names, display order) and the default staff role set with the permissions each role holds.
why: SETUP-SEED asks for staff roles and UAE denominations, but the package holds neither. shift.yaml says 'the UAE set he supplied is the seed' and quotes only a bad 'Coin, 0' row. mom-digest records the default role templates as still pending.
blocks: SETUP-SEED, and therefore every POS cash screen and every role-gated screen in test.
affects: OrderService (shift and cash), IdentityService (roles), POS
default: Notes 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 and 1000 AED; coins 25 fils, 50 fils and 1 AED. We draft cashier, supervisor, venue manager, finance and tenant admin roles from the permission list for you to correct.

question: Must a guest's ticket QR keep rotating with no signal (F50), or may the app show a static code when offline?
why: F50 says the credential 'is already on the device and rotates locally', but getEntitlementCredential returns a single server payload and nothing defines a device-side seed, time step or offline check at the gate.
blocks: GST-013 and GST-055 ticket display, and gate-side offline validation.
affects: Guest App, AccessService, gate readers
default: It rotates offline. The app holds a time-based seed fetched while online, and gates verify the code offline.

question: On the guest web, is 'buy merchandise and collect it on the way out' paid online first and then collected (shop-and-drop), or reserved unpaid and paid at collection?
why: The retail contract says reserveMerchandise holds unsold stock for someone who has not paid, and that paid goods awaiting handover are createShopAndDrop (staff-only, needs a sale). F51, WEB-033 and WEB-042 use reserve as 'reserved at purchase'. There is no path from reserve to pay to collect.
blocks: WEB-033 and WEB-042.
affects: Guest Web, RetailService, OrderService
default: Paid online at checkout, which creates the shop-and-drop for collection.

question: Does the system re-check allergen claims automatically after every recipe or substitution change, with the Verify button kept only as a manual re-check, or does staff trigger it?
why: verifyAllergens says 'Run on every recipe change, not on demand', but BO-045 and BO-111 give it a Verify button, and nothing runs it on the server.
blocks: BO-045 and BO-111.
affects: FnbService, back office menu and recipe screens
default: Automatic after every change. The Verify button stays as a manual re-check.

question: Do guests get an in-app feed of in-venue notifications (queue calls, order updates, venue notices) in the first release?
why: GST-030 and WEB-046 exist for this, but no contract has a guest operation, stream or channel that returns such notifications. CF-134 and CF-50 already record the mechanism as missing.
blocks: GST-030 and WEB-046, both scheduled in Block A.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, notification mechanism
default: Not in the first release. Take GST-030 and WEB-046 out of Block A. Queue calls and order status show on the queue and order screens that already poll for them.
superseded: The notifications-feed deferral is reversed 29 September (rev 3 GAP-C1): the in-venue notifications feed (GST-030, WEB-046) is in the first release.

question: We propose re-deriving navigation between screens so that a screen links only to screens it can pass the needed ids to, and every 'Returns to X' is mirrored on both screens. Inferred exits such as Stock Count to Queue Directory would be removed. Confirm or correct.
why: Exit lists were generated from module menus and carry parameters the source screen never holds. For example, BO-079 exits to BO-001 carrying eventId, feedId and queueId, and POS-001 never lists its child POS-017. We are fixing this ourselves, but it changes how users move between your screens.
blocks: Navigation on 228 screen tickets.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, POS, back office, White Label CMS
first_release: Yes: navigation on the Guest App, Guest Web and POS screens
default: Confirm the proposal as written.

question: Who on your side reviews and signs off the redrawn Block A wireframes, and how quickly per batch?
why: None of the 2,427 screens has a reviewed or drawn wireframe. Every one is 'notStarted' with a generated placeholder frame, so developers build without an agreed layout. We will draw the frames. Sign-off is yours.
blocks: Frontend acceptance on every Block A screen ticket.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, POS, Kitchen Display, White Label CMS, back office
default: One named design reviewer, with sign-off within 3 working days of each batch.
applied: applied 28 September, one value open: Rule recorded: one named design reviewer, sign-off within 3 working days of each batch. Missing: the reviewer's name.

question: We propose re-deriving each screen's operations from its purpose and journeys, removing those attached by name resemblance or bulk attach. For example: BO-036 Device Registry loses the guest CRM operations, BO-070 Work Orders binds maintenance work orders instead of sales orders, and ADM-412 (TICVAI fees) is separated from the venue payment gateway. Confirm or correct.
why: The screens' own notes admit the 18 August bulk attach and attachment 'by module resemblance', and the 24 August clean-up was partial. We are fixing this ourselves. Where a screen's purpose is unclear, we will follow the purpose as written unless you correct it.
blocks: Frontend build on 176 screen tickets.
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, POS, Kitchen Display, back office, Platform Console
first_release: Yes: POS-001 to POS-011, GST-002, GST-008 and other Guest App, Guest Web and POS screens
default: Confirm the proposal as written.

question: May we restore the drawn boards archived on 9 September (Seat, Retail, POS, F&B and Guest Mobile boards) as reference frames until the redrawn batches land, or are they superseded?
why: 88 screens note that their Claude Design or client-drawn frame was archived to a folder nothing reads. The screens now point at generated placeholders. Only a few P01 redraws exist so far, and the screens do not yet point at them.
blocks: Layout for the POS, Kitchen Display and back-office tickets until their batches are redrawn.
affects: POS, Kitchen Display, Guest App, back office
first_release: Yes: POS-001 to POS-020, KIT-001 to KIT-009, GST-005, GST-021, GST-049
default: Restore them as reference. Each is replaced by its redrawn frame when that batch lands.

question: For the journeys built from your board's arrows (F78, F79, F89, F95, F107), please confirm what each is meant to do. For example, F95 starts at Device Registry but walks guest-merge operations, and F78 puts production planning inside a supplier and pricing journey. Also: on a POS F&B order (F108), is it send to kitchen then charge (POS-022), or charge first?
why: These flows were built from the board's GOES TO edges, with operations picked from each screen's bulk-attached list. Their client frame references contradict the screens. F108 pays before sending, while POS-022 says 'Send to kitchen, then charge'.
blocks: Re-authoring these flows, and the POS F&B order sequence.
affects: POS, Kitchen Display, back office, White Label CMS
first_release: Yes: POS-004, POS-005, POS-022, KIT-002, KIT-003, CMS-002, CMS-003
default: Each journey follows the purpose of the screens it visits. POS F&B: send to kitchen, then charge.

question: How does the guest app know which venue the guest is at: the guest picks one (remembered), location detection, or the venue on today's ticket or deep link?
why: GuestSession has no venue, yet getWaitTimes requires venueId and several guest operations need it. Only 6 of 117 guest screens declare a venue source, all 'from: session', and a guest session holds none.
blocks: Every guest screen that shows waits, menus, offers or maps (32 tickets).
affects: Guest App, Guest Web, IdentityService (GuestSession)
first_release: Yes: GST-002 to GST-005, GST-020 to GST-023, WEB-002, WEB-015, WEB-040 and others
default: The guest picks a venue on first open, and the choice is remembered and changeable. On the day of a visit, the app suggests the venue on the guest's ticket.

question: What are the limits for: brand asset uploads (file types and maximum size; setBrandIdentity only says 'exceeds size limits'), and the allowed minimum and maximum for each connectivity policy setting on BO-131?
why: The screens need these to validate input and show errors, and the contract gives defaults only, with no bounds. The rest of this group is per-screen state writing we do ourselves.
blocks: CMS-002, CMS-004 and BO-131 validation.
affects: White Label CMS, WhiteLabelService, TenancyService
default: PNG or SVG, up to 2 MB. For connectivity, we propose bounds for you to correct.

question: For screens built from your pack PDFs, which fields are real requirements? (a) ADM-412 fee methods (Card, Bank Transfer, Other); (b) BO-161 guest categories (Adult to Accreditation) against the age and height rules; (c) BO-825 challenge actions (scan, activity, purchase); (d) BO-1045 price bands on seat categories; (e) BO-003's seven queue feed sources, including Manual; (f) BO-093 accept only, or accept, edit and reject.
why: These fields came from the pack and were never reconciled with the operations the screens call, so they bind to nothing or disagree with the contract.
affects: Platform Console, back office
default: Keep (c) and (d), and we add them to the contract. Map (b) onto age rules. Keep (f) as accept, edit and reject. (a) and (e) follow the contract unless you need them.

question: Are these separate screens or one? BO-015 and BO-016; BO-041 and BO-042; BO-058 and BO-059; CMS-015 and CMS-020; BO-036 and BO-127; BO-141 and BO-472; and BO-027, BO-320 and BO-652 (reissue).
why: Each pair carries the same or nearly the same operations, and no screen says how the work divides. BO-031 is still named 'Asset Register' after being rewired to access points.
blocks: Build of the cloned screens.
affects: Back office, White Label CMS
default: Merge BO-127 into BO-036, BO-472 into BO-141, CMS-020 into CMS-015, and BO-320 and BO-652 into BO-027. Keep BO-015/016 and BO-041/042 separate, each with its own operations.

question: On the kitchen display, do we build station load, a course filter and assigning a display to a kitchen station, or remove them from the screens?
why: All ten KIT screens carry one pasted template with station load, a Bump button and a course filter. Nothing provides station load or a course filter, and nothing assigns a device to a station, although P15 says the station resolves from the device assignment.
blocks: KIT-001 to KIT-008 build.
affects: Kitchen Display, FnbService, TenancyService (workstations)
default: Build device-to-station assignment and a course filter. Drop the station-load tile from the first release.

question: Name the eight seeded reports every venue runs, and which one each report screen shows: POS-008 terminal day view, POS-020, BO-059 sales by channel, BO-060 attendance and footfall, BO-133.
why: listSeededReports promises 'the eight reports every venue runs' but never lists them. Eight screens call runReport with no report named, and nothing returns sales by channel or aggregate attendance.
blocks: POS-008, POS-020, BO-133 and the back-office report screens.
affects: ReportingService, LedgerService, POS, back office
default: We propose the eight from the screens that need them (terminal day view, sales by channel, attendance and footfall, shift summary, refunds, voids and discounts, stock valuation, F&B sales) for you to correct.

question: Do the back-office hub screens (BO-100, BO-103 to BO-108) and the Queue Monitor (BO-005) need live counts and KPI tiles (takings, admissions, open shifts, items needing attention, called and expired parties), or can they open into sections without counts?
why: The hubs promise counts ('The count is the point'), but no operation returns them, and paged lists carry no total. getKpiValues exists but no hub declares it.
blocks: BO-100, BO-103 to BO-108 and BO-005.
affects: Back office, ReportingService, QueueService
default: Bind takings and admissions to getKpiValues. Drop the attention counts until a summary operation exists.

question: Can an archived media asset be restored to use, and can a quarantined asset be released back to ready? If yes, what ends an asset's life - only deleting it?
why: The media state model (states/media.yaml) calls ready, quarantined and archived terminal, yet updateMediaAsset moves between them (quarantined->ready, ready->archived, archived->ready). Either those states are not final or those moves should not exist; the package cannot say which.
blocks: The asset lifecycle in AssetsService and the CMS Media Library screens (CMS-010, CMS-075); check-states fails on it.
affects: assets.yaml (updateMediaAsset, deleteMediaAsset), P13 White-Label CMS media screens
first_release: Yes: White Label CMS media library
default: Restore is allowed: archived->ready and quarantined->ready (after review) stay; nothing is terminal except by deletion, which removes the row.

question: Can a cancelled subscription be reactivated (setSubscription back to active), or must the tenant start a new subscription?
why: states/subscription.yaml marks cancelled as terminal but also lists cancelled->active through setSubscription. A reactivation keeps history and entitlements on one record; a new subscription starts clean. The package records neither decision.
blocks: SubscriptionService billing and the tenant plan screens; check-states fails on it.
affects: subscription.yaml (setSubscription, cancelSubscription), P09 plan and billing screens
default: Reactivation within the paid period is allowed on the same record; after the period ends the subscription expires and a new one is required.
